items.followUp: Why is the first ionization energy of chlorine greater than that of bromine?

rubric.why: Identifies why sodium's outer electron is more strongly held.
rubric.description: Na has a smaller atomic radius, so its outer electron is closer to the nucleus than K's.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the smaller radius or closer outer electron.

rubric.why: Connects the stronger attraction to the energy needed for ionization.
rubric.description: The stronger nuclear attraction means more energy is needed to remove Na's outer electron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the stronger attraction and its effect on ionization energy.

modelAnswer: Na has a smaller atomic radius than K, so its outermost electron is closer to the nucleus and experiences less shielding.
The nucleus attracts this electron more strongly; therefore, more energy is required to remove it from Na than from K.

items.followUp: Describe how Rutherford discovered the proton and give two properties of a proton.

rubric.why: States the key experimental evidence and identification of the neutron.
rubric.description: Chadwick's 1932 experiment: alpha particles struck beryllium, and the emitted neutral radiation knocked protons from paraffin wax.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for the date/scientist, beryllium and alpha particles, and the paraffin-wax evidence.

rubric.why: Gives the neutron's defining electrical property.
rubric.description: A neutron has no electrical charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the neutron is neutral.

rubric.why: Gives the neutron's mass and location as key properties.
rubric.description: A neutron has a mass of about 1 amu, nearly equal to a proton's, and is found in the atomic nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its approximate mass and 1 mark for its location in the nucleus.

modelAnswer: In 1932, James Chadwick bombarded beryllium with alpha particles from a radioactive source.
The beryllium emitted a highly penetrating radiation that had no charge.
When this radiation struck paraffin wax, protons were ejected from the wax; Chadwick concluded that the radiation consisted of neutrons.
A neutron has no electrical charge.
Its mass is about 1 amu, nearly equal to the mass of a proton, and it is present in the nucleus of an atom.

items.followUp: Write four differences between an atom and an ion.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a molecule from a charged molecular ion by net charge.
rubric.description: A molecule is electrically neutral.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a molecule has no net charge.

rubric.why: States the defining charge of a molecular ion.
rubric.description: A molecular ion is a group of bonded atoms with a net positive or negative charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a molecular ion has a net charge.

rubric.why: Explains the difference in charge in terms of electron and proton numbers.
rubric.description: A molecule has equal numbers of protons and electrons; a molecular ion has unequal numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the proton/electron distinction.

rubric.why: Provides examples that illustrate the two categories.
rubric.description: Examples include H₂O or CO₂ for molecules and NH₄⁺, SO₄²⁻ or NO₃⁻ for molecular ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example of each category.

modelAnswer: A molecule is a group of atoms joined by chemical bonds and has no net charge; a molecular ion is a bonded group of atoms carrying a net charge.
A molecule has equal numbers of protons and electrons; a molecular ion has unequal numbers of protons and electrons.
Molecules are written without an overall charge, whereas molecular ions are written with a positive or negative charge, such as NH₄⁺ or SO₄²⁻.
Examples: H₂O is a molecule, while NH₄⁺ is a molecular ion.

items.followUp: Define a covalent bond and explain its formation in a hydrogen molecule.

rubric.why: Defines ionic bonding as electron transfer followed by attraction between ions.
rubric.description: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed after electron transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for electron transfer and 1 mark for electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

rubric.why: Explains the electron transfer and resulting ions in the example.
rubric.description: In sodium chloride, sodium transfers one electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the transfer from sodium to chlorine and 1 mark for correctly identifying the ions.

rubric.why: Connects the ions' attraction to formation of the ionic compound.
rubric.description: The attraction between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ forms the ionic compound NaCl.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the ionic attraction producing sodium chloride.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by the transfer of electrons.
For example, a sodium atom transfers its outermost electron to a chlorine atom.
Sodium becomes a positive ion, Na⁺, and chlorine becomes a negative ion, Cl⁻.
The oppositely charged ions attract each other and form the ionic compound sodium chloride, NaCl.

items.followUp: Describe dilute, concentrated, saturated and unsaturated solutions, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Defines a dilute solution by its relatively small amount of dissolved solute.
rubric.description: A dilute solution contains a relatively small amount of solute compared with the solvent or solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition and/or an appropriate example.

rubric.why: Defines a concentrated solution by its relatively large amount of dissolved solute.
rubric.description: A concentrated solution contains a relatively large amount of solute compared with the solvent or solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition and/or an appropriate example.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a saturated solution by its solubility limit at a given temperature.
rubric.description: A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a particular temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition and/or an appropriate example.

rubric.why: Distinguishes an unsaturated solution from a saturated one.
rubric.description: An unsaturated solution can still dissolve more solute at the same temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition and/or an appropriate example.

modelAnswer: A dilute solution contains a relatively small amount of solute; for example, a small amount of sugar dissolved in water.
A concentrated solution contains a relatively large amount of solute; for example, a large amount of sugar dissolved in water.
A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a solvent at a particular temperature; for example, saturated salt water.
An unsaturated solution can dissolve more solute at that temperature; for example, salt water to which more salt can still be added and dissolved.
